newsitem.title: USA: SEC hands NYS Senator's study to market regulators.
newsitem.headline: SEC hands NYS Senator's study to market regulators.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has told a New York State Senator, who linked political gifts by bond firms to their success in getting contracts, that his study would go to its market regulators.

Arthur Levitt Jr., the SEC chairman, said in the letter, "I look forward to receiving a copy of the report mentioned in your letter, which I will share with our Division of Market Regulation and Office of Municipal Securities."
The response was contained in a letter dated April 15 that was sent to the New York State Senator.

A spokesman for Senator Franz Leichter said on Wednesday that the report had been provided to the SEC by the Democrat state Senator from Manhattan, and that this was the only letter the senator had received from the SEC.

New York State Gov George Pataki was attacked by Leichter for benefiting from big donations made by municipal bond underwriters who got profitable contracts. He accused state Republicans of violating the spirt, if not the letter, of SEC rul G-37, which he said prohibits firms from making donations to state officials within two years of winning any negotiated municipal securities business in the state.

The report by Leichter is on the agenda of the next board meeting of the rule-making body for the municipal securities industry. The Municipal Securities Rule-Making Board next meets on April 30 to May 1 in Washington.
